recipe.label: Ink Wash

traits.medium: restrained grayscale ink-wash cloud landscape on absorbent paper
traits.texture: diluted ink gradients, expressive soft bleed edges and selective dark accents
traits.composition: leave generous light paper for bright cloud lobes; preserve the large shadow masses and open sky
traits.lighting: tonal atmosphere using paper light and layered gray washes

review_checks: restrained washes without dense decorative outlines
limitations: Wash edges and tonal detail may drift during edits; physical ink diffusion is not simulated.
Palette and fine geometry are prompt guidance and require visual review across a series.

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: README style reference; intended use: One reviewed Ink Wash example for the Art Skill style catalog
Primary request: A towering white cumulus cloud with bright sunlit upper-right lobes and cool shadowed lower-left volumes, rising into a large deep-blue sky. Tiny dark foliage and roofline details sit only along the bottom edge.
Style/medium: restrained grayscale ink-wash cloud landscape on absorbent paper
Color palette: #F4F0E6, #A9AAA5, #666D70, #30383B
Materials/textures: diluted ink gradients, expressive soft bleed edges and selective dark accents
Composition/framing: leave generous light paper for bright cloud lobes; preserve the large shadow masses and open sky; Keep portrait orientation and the original broad framing; one image, no frame or panels
Lighting/mood: tonal atmosphere using paper light and layered gray washes
Requested output target: 1024x1536, opaque background, png; use only supported tool controls
Avoid: real people; copyrighted characters; logos and brand marks; copied artworks; unrequested lettering
Constraints: Keep the original upward sky viewpoint, large lobed cloud shape, light/shadow arrangement and broad upper sky. Foreground remains a small lower-edge suggestion. Do not add a sea, island bay, garden, sunset or rainbow.; No added people, brands, characters, captions or signatures; Use only this source photograph as the composition reference; never mix motifs from the other photos
